collection_summary: This instance is an exhaustive historical slice over a single source-defined accession list. It uses the explicit country-year list of eurozone entrants on the Wikipedia page 'Enlargement of the eurozone' and keeps only entrants from 1999 through 2023.
source_coverage_notes: The cited page explicitly states that the first 11 eurozone members introduced the euro on 1 January 1999, then names Greece (2001), Slovenia (2007), Cyprus and Malta (2008), Slovakia (2009), Estonia (2011), Latvia (2014), Lithuania (2015), Croatia (2023), and Bulgaria (2026). This instance keeps all countries in that explicit historical list through 2023 and excludes only Bulgaria because it falls outside the query range. Roles: source_urls[0] (Enlargement_of_the_eurozone): universe + value - it both defines the closed accession set (which countries are in scope) and supplies every Adoption Year cell; no other source is needed to populate any row or cell. The Wikipedia 'Eurozone' overview page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurozone) was consulted informally as a cross-check during audit (it independently confirms the 20-member in-range count, that Croatia is the 20th member, and each per-country year) but is NOT added to source_urls: per the artifact-contract source-role convention, validation/cross-check sources live in this prose and do not count toward source_count.
decision_log: Chose a single-source temporal instance as a forward test of the curation skill because it is easier to verify than a multi-source fuzzy-join case while still adding a new benchmark category not present in cfg.json. The initial 2001-2023 draft had only 9 rows and failed the protocol minimum-row criterion, so the query was widened to 1999-2023. Marked the claim type as exhaustive because the source text itself is an explicit historical accession list rather than a 'major examples' subset. CYCLE-2 CURATOR REPAIR (resolving the lone cycle-1 claude-code SUGGESTION S1): the auditor optionally proposed adding the Wikipedia 'Eurozone' page as a validation-role source. DECISION: keep source_count=1 and do NOT add a second URL. Rationale: (a) the single cited 'Enlargement of the eurozone' page is the dedicated accession-history page and fully supports both the exhaustive in-range membership list AND every Adoption Year cell - it carries the universe + value roles by itself, so nothing in the CSV is ungrounded; (b) the artifact-contract source-role convention is explicit that validation/cross-check sources do NOT count toward source_count and must live in source_coverage_notes prose, not in source_urls - so promoting the 'Eurozone' overview page into source_urls and bumping source_count would actually violate the contract and add a redundant counted source purely to silence an optional suggestion, which SKILL.md severity guidance discourages; (c) the 'Eurozone' page was nonetheless used as an informal audit cross-check and is now named in source_coverage_notes for provenance. This closes SUGGESTION S1 as resolved-by-decision under current Wiki-primary policy.
normalization_decisions: Country names follow the source page's English article names. Adoption years are stored as bare integers. The table uses Country as the primary key because each country appears once in the filtered historical slice.
open_questions: RESOLVED in cycle-2: the cycle-1 suggestion to add a second (validation-role) Wikipedia source was considered and declined - see decision_log; source_count stays 1 and the cross-check source is documented in source_coverage_notes prose only. Remaining (non-blocking) forward note: if later benchmark policy prefers only sources more authoritative than Wikipedia for treaty-history questions, this instance could be rebuilt from EU or ECB historical accession materials. Otherwise the current single Wikipedia source is sufficient for a stable, easily auditable temporal benchmark item.
